subject: Math
prompt:
Which of the following must be a factor of the expression $3x^{2} - (6 + 7r)x + 14r$ for every nonzero value of $r$?

I. $3x - 7r$

II. $x - 2r$
explanation: Choice A is correct. To factor $3x^2 - (6 + 7r)x + 14r$, first distribute the middle term: $3x^2 - 6x - 7rx + 14r$. Group the terms: $(3x^2 - 6x) + (-7rx + 14r)$. Factor each group: $3x(x - 2) - 7r(x - 2)$. Factor out the common binomial: $(3x - 7r)(x - 2)$. Factor I, $3x - 7r$, is always a factor. Factor II, $x - 2r$, matches the factor $x - 2$ only in the special case $r = 1$, so it is not a factor that must appear for every nonzero value of $r$. Therefore, only I must be a factor.
